title: Rama spoke to Matali
introduction: Seeing Ravana's chariot coming, Rama asks Matali the charioteer to be on his guard. Bad omens prognosticating the fall of Ravana and good omens predicting the victory of Rama appeared in the scene of battle-field.
closing: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे आदिकाव्ये युद्धकाण्डे षडुत्तरशततमः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 106th chapter in Yuddha Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
सारथिः स रथम् हृष्टं परसैन्यप्रधर्षणम् |
गन्धर्वनगराकारं समुच्छ्रितपाताकिनम्
युक्तं परमसंपन्नैर्वाइभिर्हेममालिभिः |
युद्धोपकरणैः पूर्णं पताकाध्वजमालिनम्
ग्रसन्तमिव चाकाशं नादयन्तं वसुंधराम् |
प्रणाशं परनैन्यानां स्वनैन्यस्य प्रहर्षणम्
रावणस्य रथं क्षिप्रं चोदयामास सारथिः |
verses.iast:
sārathiḥ sa ratham hṛṣṭaṃ parasainyapradharṣaṇam |
gandharvanagarākāraṃ samucchritapātākinam
yuktaṃ paramasampannairvāibhirhemamālibhiḥ |
yuddhopakaraṇaiḥ pūrṇaṃ patākādhvajamālinam
grasantamiva cākāśaṃ nādayantaṃ vasundharām |
praṇāśaṃ paranainyānāṃ svanainyasya praharṣaṇam
rāvaṇasya rathaṃ kṣipraṃ codayāmāsa sārathiḥ |
verses.translation: Thrilling with rapture, that charioteer, the charioteer of Ravana, drove forward quickly, his chariot, a chariot, which was capable of attacking the army of enemies, a wonderful piece of art like Gandharva-city, an imaginary city in the sky, mounted with flags, yoked with horses of excellent quality adorned with golden necklaces, filled with war-implements, adorned with rows of flags and banners, which was devouring the sky as it were, making the earth resound, which was the destroyer of the army of adversaries and caused delight to its own.

glosses.meaning: which attacked the army of enemies
which was in form of Gandharva-city

verses.devanagari:
तमापतन्तन् सहसा स्वनवन्तं महाध्वजम्
रथन् राक्षसराजस्य नरराजो ददर्श ह |
कृष्णवाजिसमायुक्तन् युक्तं रौद्रेण वर्चसा
दीप्यमानमिवाकाशे विमानं सूर्यवर्चसं |
तडित्पताकागहनन् दर्शितेन्द्रायुधायुधम्
verses.iast:
tamāpatantan sahasā svanavantaṃ mahādhvajam
rathan rākṣasarājasya nararājo dadarśa ha |
kṛṣṇavājisamāyuktan yuktaṃ raudreṇa varcasA
dīpyamānamivākāśe vimānaṃ sūryavarcasaṃ |
taḍitpatākāgahanan darśitendrāyudhāyudham
verses.translation: Rama saw that Ravana's chariot, which was coming speedily with a noise, bearing a large flag-staff, yoked with black horses, endowed with a terrific luster, blazing like an aerial car in the sky, with a luster of the sun, filled with lightning-like flags and with a beautiful appearance of a rain-bow.

glosses.meaning: with a luster of the sun
and with a beautiful appearance of a rain-bow.

verses.devanagari:
शरधारा विमुञ्चन्तन् धारासारमिवान्बुदम् |
तन् दृष्ट्वा मेघसङ्काशमापतन्तन् रथं रिपोः
गिरेर्वज्राभिमृष्टस्य दीर्यतः सदृशस्वनम् |
विस्पारयन्वै वेगेन बालचन्द्रानतं धनुः
उवाच मातलिन् रामः सहस्राक्षस्य मातलिम् |
verses.iast:
śaradhārā vimuñcantan dhārāsāramivānbudam |
tan dṛṣṭvā meghasañkāśamāpatantan rathaṃ ripoḥ
girervajrābhimṛṣṭasya dIryataḥ sadṛśasvanam |
vispārayanvai vegena bālacandrānataṃ dhanuḥ
uvāca mātalin rāmaḥ sahasrākṣasya mātalim |
verses.translation: Seeing that chariot, releasing streams of arrows, like a cloud releasing streams of rain, with a noise equal to that of a bursting mountain, struck with a diamond, Rama after stretching his bow in a crescent shape, spoke to Matali, Indra's charioteer as follows:

glosses.meaning: with a noise equal to that

verses.devanagari:
मातले पश्य सन्रब्धमापतन्तन् रथं रिपोः
यथापसव्यं पतता वेगेन महता पुनः |
समरे हन्तुमात्मानन् तथानेन कृता मतिः
verses.iast:
mātale paśya sanrabdhamāpatantan rathaṃ ripoḥ
yathāpasavyaṃ patatā vegena mahatā punaḥ |
samare hantumātmānan tathānena kṛtā matiḥ
verses.translation: "O Matali! From the way in which the enemy is marching forward from left to right with a great speed in his chariot more, it appears that heart has been set by him upon destroying himself in the battle."

glosses.meaning: from the right to the left

verses.devanagari:
तदप्रमादमातिष्ठ प्रत्युद्गच्छ रथन् रिपोः|
विध्वन्सयितुमिच्छामि वायुर्मेघमिवोत्थितम्
verses.iast:
tadapramādamātiṣṭha pratyudgaccha rathan ripoḥ |
vidhvansayitumicchāmi vāyurmeghamivotthitam
verses.translation: "Therefore, take care and march forward, facing the chariot of the enemy I wish to destroy it, even as the wind would blow a cloud."

verses.devanagari:
अविक्लवमसम्भ्रान्तमव्यग्रहृदयेक्षणम् |
रश्मिसञ्चारनियतं प्रचोदय रथन् द्रुतम्
verses.iast:
aviklavamasambhrāntamavyagrahṛdayekṣaṇam |
raśmisañcāraniyataṃ pracodaya rathan drutam
verses.translation: "Without fear and flurry and with a steady heart and vision, and the movement of the reins fully controlled, drive the chariot swiftly."

glosses.meaning: and the move of the reins fully controlled

verses.devanagari:
कामं न त्वन् समाधेयः पुरन्दररथोचितः |
युयुत्सुरहमेकाग्रः स्मारये त्वां न शिक्षये
verses.iast:
kāmaṃ na tvan samādheyaḥ purandararathocitaḥ |
yuyutsurahamekāgraḥ smāraye tvāṃ na śikṣaye
verses.translation: "You need not be instructed by me, accustomed as you are to drive the chariot of Indra the lord of celestials. Keen as I am to fight with a close attention, I am just reminding you and not teaching you."

glosses.meaning: accustomed as you are to drive the chariot of Indra the lord of celestials
keen as I am to fight
with a close attention smaaraye = I am just reminding

verses.devanagari:
परितुष्टः स रामस्य तेन वाक्येन मातलिः |
प्रचोदयामास रथन् सुरसारथिसत्तमः
verses.iast:
parituṣṭaḥ sa rāmasya tena vākyena mātaliḥ |
pracodayāmāsa rathan surasārathisattamaḥ
verses.translation: Extremely gratified with those words of Rama, that Matali the excellent charioteer of gods drove on the chariot.

verses.devanagari:
अपसव्यन् ततः कुर्वन्रावणस्य महारथम् |
चक्रोत्क्षिप्तेन रजसा रावणन् व्यवधूनयत्
verses.iast:
apasavyan tataḥ kurvanrāvaṇasya mahāratham |
cakrotkṣiptena rajasā rāvaṇan vyavadhUnayat
verses.translation: Passing the huge chariot of Ravana on the right, the charioteer then set Ravana shaking, by the dust risen from the wheels of his own chariot.

glosses.meaning: by the dust risen from the wheels (of his own chariot).

verses.devanagari:
ततः क्रुद्धो दशग्रीवस्ताम्रविस्फारितेक्षणः |
रथप्रतिमुखन् रामं सायकैरवधूनयत्
verses.iast:
tataḥ kruddho daśagrIvastāmravisphāritekṣaṇaḥ |
rathapratimukhan rāmaṃ sāyakairavadhUnayat
verses.translation: The enraged Ravana then, with his coppery eyes wide open, trembled Rama, who stood facing his chariot, with arrows.

glosses.meaning: with his coppery eyes wide open

verses.devanagari:
धर्षणामर्षितो रामो धैर्यन् रोषेण लङ्घयन् |
जग्राह सुमहावेगमैन्द्रन् युधि शरासनम्
verses.iast:
dharṣaṇāmarṣito rāmo dhairyan roṣeṇa lañghayan |
jagrāha sumahāvegamaindran yudhi śarāsanam
verses.translation: Meeting fortitude with anger, though provoked with assault, Rama took hold of Indra's bow, which was possessed of extra ordinary impulse in the battle-field.

glosses.meaning: which was possessed of extra ordinary impulse

verses.devanagari:
शरांश्च सुमहातेजाः सूर्यरश्मिसमप्रभान् |
तदुपोढं महद्युद्धमन्योन्यवधकाङ्क्षिणोः
परस्पराभिमुखयोर्दृप्तयोरिव सिन्हयोः |
verses.iast:
śarāṃśca sumahātejāḥ sUryaraśmisamaprabhān |
tadupoḍhaṃ mahadyuddhamanyonyavadhakāñkṣiṇoḥ
parasparābhimukhayordṛptayoriva sinhayoḥ |
verses.translation: He also seized hold of arrows of exceeding swiftness, which were shining like sun-beams. Then began that great battle between the two warriors (Rama and Ravana) who were desirous of killing each other, while facing each other like two proud lions.

glosses.meaning: he also seized hold of arrows
between the two warriors (Rama and Ravana) who wee desirous of killing each other
and who were facing each other

verses.devanagari:
ततो देवाः सगन्धर्वाः सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः
समीयुर्द्वैरथन् द्रष्टुन् रावणक्षयकाङ्क्षिणः |
verses.iast:
tato devāḥ sagandharvāḥ siddhāśca paramarṣayaḥ
samIyurdvairathan draṣṭun rāvaṇakṣayakāñkṣiṇaḥ |
verses.translation: Then, the gods along with the Gandharvas the celestial musicians, Siddhas the demigods and great sages, desirous of Ravana's ruin, arrived to see the battle of both the chariot-warrriors.

glosses.meaning: along with Gandharvas the celestial musicians
the battle of both the chariot-warriors.

verses.devanagari:
समुत्पेतुरथोत्पाता दारुणा लोमहर्षणाः
रावणस्य विनाशाय राघवस्य जयाय च |
verses.iast:
samutpeturathotpātā dāruṇā lomaharṣaṇāḥ
rāvaṇasya vināśāya rāghavasya jayāya ca |
verses.translation: Thereupon, terrific portents that caused one's hair to stand on end, appeared giving an augury of doom to Ravana and prosperity to Rama.

glosses.meaning: that caused one's hair to stand on end
giving an augury of doom to Ravana

verses.devanagari:
ववर्ष रुधिरन् देवो रावणस्य रथोपरि
वाता मण्डलिनस्तीव्रा अपसव्यं प्रचक्रमुः |
verses.iast:
vavarṣa rudhiran devo rāvaṇasya rathopari
vātā maṇḍalinastIvrā apasavyaṃ pracakramuḥ |
verses.translation: The god of rains poured blood on Ravana's chariot. Horrible winds blew from right to left, forming circles.

verses.devanagari:
महद् गृध्रकुलन् चास्य भ्रममाणं नभस्तले
येन येन रथो याति तेन तेन प्रधावति |
verses.iast:
mahad gṛdhrakulan cāsya bhramamāṇaṃ nabhastale
yena yena ratho yāti tena tena pradhāvati |
verses.translation: A large flock of vultures, roaming about in the sky, was flying forward in the same direction in which Ravana's chariot was going.

verses.devanagari:
सन्ध्यया चावृता लङ्का जपापुष्पनिकाशया
दृश्यते सम्प्रदीतेव दिवसेअपि वसुन्धरा |
verses.iast:
sandhyayā cāvṛtA lañkā japāpuṣpanikāśayā
dṛśyate sampradIteva divaseapi vasundharā |
verses.translation: Lanka was overcast with dusk, resembling a (red) Japa flower. The land in Lanka, as also the day appeared as if they were blazing.

verses.devanagari:
सनिर्घाता महोल्काश्च सम्प्रचेतुर्महास्वनाः
विषादयन्त्यो रक्षान्सि रावणस्य तदाहिताः |
verses.iast:
sanirghātā maholkāśca sampraceturmahāsvanāḥ
viṣādayantyo rakṣānsi rāvaṇasya tadāhitāḥ |
verses.translation: Large meteors, along with lightnings fell with great noise. Those entities, inimical to Ravana, made demons to lament.

verses.devanagari:
रावणश्च यतस्तत्र प्रचचाल वसुन्धरा
रक्षसान् च प्रहरतां गृहीता इव बाहवः |
verses.iast:
rāvaṇaśca yatastatra pracacāla vasundharā
rakṣasān ca praharatāṃ gṛhItā iva bāhavaḥ |
verses.translation: The earth on which Ravana was there, trembled. The arms of fighting demons looked as if they were clasped.

glosses.meaning: were like as if they were clasped.

verses.devanagari:
ताम्राः पीताः सिताः श्वेताः पतिताः सूर्यरश्मयः
दृश्यन्ते रावणस्याङ्गे पर्वतस्येव धातवः |
verses.iast:
tāmrāḥ pItāḥ sitāḥ śvetāḥ patitāḥ sUryaraśmayaḥ
dṛśyante rāvaṇasyāñge parvatasyeva dhātavaḥ |
verses.translation: Fallen before Ravana, the rays of the sun appeared coppery, yellow, white and dark, like mineral ores on a mountain.

verses.devanagari:
गृध्रैरनुगताश्चास्य वमन्त्यो ज्वलनं मुखैः
प्रणेदुर्मुखमीक्षन्त्यः सन्रब्धमशिवन् शिवाः |
verses.iast:
gṛdhrairanugatāścāsya vamantyo jvalanaṃ mukhaiḥ
praṇedurmukhamIkṣantyaḥ sanrabdhamaśivan śivāḥ |
verses.translation: The she-jackals followed by vultures hastily uttered inauspicious howls, on beholding Ravana's face as also vomiting fire from their mouths.

verses.devanagari:
प्रतिकूलन् ववौ वायू रणे पान्सून् समुत्किरन्
तस्य राक्षसराजस्य कुर्वन्दृष्टिविलोपनम् |
verses.iast:
pratikUlan vavau vāyU raṇe pānsUn samutkiran
tasya rākṣasarājasya kurvandṛṣṭivilopanam |
verses.translation: Scattering the dust upwards over the battle-field and clouding the vision of that Ravana, the wind blew in a direction inimicable to him.

verses.devanagari:
निपेतुरिन्द्राशनयः सैन्ये चास्य समन्ततः
दुर्विषह्य स्वना घोरा विना जलधरस्वनम् |
verses.iast:
nipeturindrāśanayaḥ sainye cāsya samantataḥ
durviṣahya svanā ghorā vinā jaladharasvanam |
verses.translation: Even without the appearance of clouds, thunderbolts fell on his army on all sides, with a noise which was hard to endure.

glosses.meaning: even without the appearance of clouds

verses.devanagari:
दिशश्च प्रदिशः सर्वा बभूवुस्तिमिरावृताः
पान्सुवर्षेण महता दुर्दर्शन् च नभोअभवत् |
verses.iast:
diśaśca pradiśaḥ sarvā babhUvustimirāvṛtāḥ
pānsuvarṣeṇa mahatā durdarśan ca nabhoabhavat |
verses.translation: All the quarters and intermediate points of the compass became covered with darkness and due to outpourings of dust, the sky became difficult to be seen.

glosses.meaning: and intermediate points of the compass
and due to outpourings of dust

verses.devanagari:
कुर्वन्त्यः कलहन् घोरन् सारिकास्तद्रथं प्रति
निपेतुः शतशस्तत्र दारुणा दारुणस्वनाः |
verses.iast:
kurvantyaḥ kalahan ghoran sārikāstadrathaṃ prati
nipetuḥ śataśastatra dāruṇā dāruṇasvanāḥ |
verses.translation: Hundreds of dreadful Sarika* birds, with their awful howls, terribly fighting there, fell down upon Ravana's chariot.

verses.devanagari:
जघनेभ्यः स्फुलिङ्गांश्च नेत्रेभ्योअश्रूणि सन्ततम्
मुमुचुस्तस्य तुरगास्तुल्यमग्निन् च वारि च |
verses.iast:
jaghanebhyaḥ sphuliñgāṃśca netrebhyoaśrUṇi santatam
mumucustasya turagāstulyamagnin ca vāri ca |
verses.translation: His horses discharged sparks of fire from their hips and loins as also tears from their eyes, releasing out fire and water at the same time continuously.

verses.devanagari:
एवं प्रकारा बहवः समुत्पाता भयावहाः
रावणस्य विनाशाय दारुणाः सम्प्रजजिञिरे |
verses.iast:
evaṃ prakārā bahavaḥ samutpātā bhayāvahāḥ
rāvaṇasya vināśāya dāruṇāḥ samprajajiJṇire |
verses.translation: Frightful portents in multitude thus sprang up, bringing danger and destruction to Ravana.

verses.devanagari:
रामस्यापि निमित्तानि सौम्यानि च शिवानि च
बभूवुर्जयशन्सीनि प्रादुर्भूतानि सर्वशः |
verses.iast:
rāmasyāpi nimittāni saumyāni ca śivāni ca
babhUvurjayaśansIni prādurbhUtāni sarvaśaḥ |
verses.translation: Pleasant and auspicious omens, depicting victory of Rama appeared on all sides, before Rama.

verses.devanagari:
निमित्तानि च सौम्यानि राघवः स्वजयाय वै
दृष्ट्वा परमसंहृष्टो हतं मेने च रावणम् |
verses.iast:
nimittāni ca saumyāni rāghavaḥ svajayāya vai
dṛṣṭvā paramasaṃhṛṣṭo hataṃ mene ca rāvaṇam |
verses.translation: Seeing the pleasant omens depicting his victory, Rama was very much pleased and considered Ravana as (already) dead.

verses.devanagari:
ततो निरीक्ष्यात्मगतानि राघवो |
रणे निमित्तानि निमित्तकोविदः |
जगाम हर्षन् च परां च निर्वृतिं |
चकार युद्धेअभ्यधिकन् च विक्रमम्
verses.iast:
tato nirIkṣyātmagatāni rāghavo |
raṇe nimittāni nimittakovidaḥ |
jagāma harṣan ca parāṃ ca nirvṛtiṃ |
cakāra yuddheabhyadhikan ca vikramam
verses.translation: Then Rama, with the knowledge of all omens, having seen those portents in his own way in the battle-field, obtained rejoice as well as extreme happiness and shown enhanced prowess in combat.

glosses.meaning: having a knowledge of the omens
